findings.title: h2 headings render at 4 different sizes
findings.evidence: “Email reimagined. Available today.” is 77px while “Test mode” is 20px (3.84×). Sizes seen: 20px ×4, 24px ×1, 56px ×8, 77px ×1. Same semantic level should get the same treatment.
findings.fix: Pick one size for h2 and set it once in CSS. If one of these is really a sub-heading, change its tag instead of its size.
findings.citation: UICrit: elements at the same level of hierarchy should get similar graphic treatment (Duan et al., UIST '24)

findings.title: Card is far taller than its content
findings.evidence: div.disable-children-scrolling.z-20 is 1022×500px but its content occupies 33% of that; 126px of empty space sits under the last line. Nothing inside it needs the height, so a fixed height or min-height is probably set.
findings.fix: Remove the fixed height / min-height and let the card size to its content, or fill the space with something that earns it.
findings.citation: Lin 2004: whitespace helps comprehension when it frames content; dead space inside a container just reads as unfinished

findings.title: Gradient-filled text (11)
findings.evidence: h1.effect-font-styling.font-domaine “Email fordevelopers” uses background-clip: text with a gradient. Decorative, hurts contrast, and reads as generated.
findings.fix: Use a solid colour. Emphasis comes from size and weight, not a rainbow.
findings.citation: Impeccable gradient-text

findings.title: Rounded icon tile above 3 headings
findings.evidence: 3 near-square 40px boxes with a background sit directly above headings. The icon-in-a-tinted-square above every feature title is the default generated feature grid.
findings.fix: Remove the tile backgrounds and let the icon sit inline with the heading, or drop the icons and let the headings carry the row.
findings.citation: Impeccable icon-tile-stack (Apache-2.0)

findings.title: Overused font
findings.evidence: “Primary font: helvetica”
findings.fix: Inter, Roboto, Fraunces, Geist, Plus Jakarta Sans, and Space Grotesk are used on so many sites they no longer feel distinctive. Each new wave of AI-generated UIs converges on the same handful of faces. Choose a face that gives your interface personality.
findings.citation: Impeccable detector (Apache-2.0, pbakaus/impeccable)

findings.title: A lone badge “delivered” that does nothing
findings.evidence: A 72×28px pill that is not clickable, is not one of a set of tags, and labels something the surrounding text already makes clear. Badges imply a category system; a single one is decoration.
findings.fix: Delete it. If the information matters, fold it into the sentence next to it. Reserve pills for things that are actually one of several (filters, statuses, tags you can click).
findings.citation: no-slop ‘status pill with dot’ heuristic (MIT); Fountain Institute tell #7 (status dots)

findings.title: 5 cards nested inside other cards
findings.evidence: 3 outer containers with bordered/shadowed children, e.g. div.disable-children-scrolling.z-20 inside div.relative.w-full. Every layer of box is a layer the reader has to look through.
findings.fix: Remove the inner border/background and separate items with spacing or a divider. One container per idea.
findings.citation: UXly nested-panel (MIT); Fountain Institute tell #5; Reinecke 2013: visual complexity is the strongest negative predictor of appeal

findings.title: 42 rounded panels on one page
findings.evidence: Rounded corners on every container is one of the ranked vibe-coded tells (#5 in the Reddit corpus).
findings.fix: Round the things that are interactive or elevated; let sections and layout containers stay square.
findings.citation: vibecoded-design-tells (MIT), tell #5

findings.title: AI purple / purple-to-blue gradient accent
findings.evidence: 1 element use a violet/indigo accent (hue 260–310°), 1 as a gradient, e.g. span.inline.leading-[0] “tonight”. This is the single most-cited vibe-coded tell in the Reddit corpus (#2 overall).
findings.fix: Pick one base hue that means something for this product and derive the palette from it. If you keep purple, make it a decision: one accent, solid, used sparingly.
findings.citation: Impeccable ai-color-palette (Apache-2.0); vibecoded-design-tells #2–3

findings.title: Dark mode with no light alternative
findings.evidence: Body background rgb(0, 0, 0) and no prefers-color-scheme rule in the CSS. Permanent dark was on 20% of Show HN launches; it's the default "techy" look, not a decision.
findings.fix: Not wrong by itself. If dark is the brand, keep it and make the rest deliberate; otherwise offer light, or default to it.
findings.citation: Krebs 2026 (20.3%); slop-detect perma_dark_mode

findings.title: Fake macOS window dots
findings.evidence: Three red/yellow/green circles drawn in CSS to make a box look like a terminal or app window. Generated UIs use it to frame fake screenshots.
findings.fix: Show a real screenshot of the real thing, or a plain code block.
findings.citation: slop-detect fake_macos_terminal

findings.title: Blurred colour blobs behind the content (6)
findings.evidence: div.center.pointer-events-none is a radial-gradient wash. The aurora backdrop is the default "atmosphere" of generated heroes.
findings.fix: Remove it and let the content carry the first screen. If you want atmosphere, use one real image.
findings.citation: slop-detect aurora_mesh_gradient; Fountain Institute tell #2

findings.title: 1 marketing buzzword
findings.evidence: “…growth acro Email reimagined.Available today.…”
findings.fix: Replace each with the specific thing: what it does, for whom, with a number if you have one. 'Streamline your workflow' → 'Turns a 40-minute export into a button.'
findings.citation: Impeccable marketing-buzzword list (Apache-2.0)

findings.title: h3 is used at 2 sizes, consistently
findings.evidence: Sizes: 16px ×3, 20px ×9. “Proactive blocklist tracking” is 20px, “Intuitive analytics” is 16px. Each size is used more than once, so this is a system rather than drift; but it means the same tag is doing two jobs.
findings.fix: If the 16px ones are sub-sections, make them h4. Screen readers and search engines only see the tag.
findings.citation: UICrit: elements at the same level of hierarchy should get similar graphic treatment (Duan et al., UIST '24)

findings.title: 3 status dots on the page
findings.evidence: Coloured dots attached to labels where a word would say more.
findings.fix: Replace with text or remove.
findings.citation: Fountain Institute tell #7
